response.title: which power station runs a fan all night for the most nights
response.answer:
If your goal is to run a fan for 8 hours every night for as many nights as possible without recharging, the most important specification is the power station's battery capacity (Wh), not its advertised wattage (W).

For example, assuming a typical 40W fan, 8 hours per night, and 85% usable battery energy:

Battery capacity

	

Estimated nights




1,000 Wh

	

2.7 nights




2,000 Wh

	

5.3 nights




3,600 Wh

	

9.6 nights




6,000 Wh

	

15.9 nights




12,000 Wh

	

31.9 nights

These estimates assume the fan plugs into an AC outlet. A more efficient 15W DC fan could last much longer.

Best power stations for maximum nights

EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X 7.2/12kw 12kWh Portable Power Stat…

Longest of these base configurations

12,000 Wh — approximately 31 nights

Listed at $7,899.00. Expandable for even longer runtime.

EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra

6,144 Wh — approximately 16 nights

Listed at $5,143.00. Supports additional battery modules.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra

3,072 Wh — approximately 8 nights

Listed at $1,299.00. More practical if you only need to power a fan.

One important consideration: large power stations can consume substantial energy just keeping their AC inverter running. For example, independent testing measured roughly 58W of idle consumption on the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus. Actual runtimes can therefore be considerably shorter than the simplified estimates above.

markup:
If your goal is to **run a fan for 8 hours every night for as many nights as possible without recharging**, the most important specification is the power station's **battery capacity (Wh)**, not its advertised wattage (W).

For example, assuming a typical 40W fan, 8 hours per night, and 85% usable battery energy:

| Battery capacity | Estimated nights |
|---|---:|
| 1,000 Wh | 2.7 nights |
| 2,000 Wh | 5.3 nights |
| 3,600 Wh | 9.6 nights |
| 6,000 Wh | 15.9 nights |
| 12,000 Wh | 31.9 nights |

These estimates assume the fan plugs into an AC outlet. A more efficient 15W DC fan could last much longer.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(40)}
{@body const [hours,setHours] = DIL.useState(8)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("3072")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Fan power consumption**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts} W</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={5} max={100} step={5} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Hours per night**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{hours} hours</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={4} max={12} step={1} value={hours} onChange={setHours}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Battery capacity</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
      <radio value="1024">1,024 Wh</radio>
      <radio value="3072">3,072 Wh</radio>
      <radio value="6144">6,144 Wh</radio>
      <radio value="12000">12,000 Wh</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime at 85% usable energy</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(Number(capacity)*0.85/(watts*hours)).toFixed(1)} nights</title>
    <caption>Before additional low-load inverter overhead</caption>
  </box>
</box>

**One question:** Are you running a regular plug-in fan (AC), or a USB-powered fan? That makes a huge difference in which power station will last the most nights.
